_doc: What the folder sidebar actually has to draw, as data, so test-mail-folder-sidebar.sh asserts against real names instead of invented ones. Never hardcode this list into the test (FIRE RULE #4).
_doc_synced: Measured on 2026-09-09 against the live account via cloud-mail-mcp mail_list_folders. These are the folders the account SYNCS - the built-in five are the short ones; the long ones are the user's own 'Fx  <emoji> <topic>' scheme, and they are what wraps. unseen is carried because the drawer appends the unread count to the label (R.string.inbox_folder_unread, '%1$s  (%2$d)'), so the string measured must be the string drawn.
_doc_builtin: The longest folder_* string in each locale the app ships. A role folder is drawn from the string resource, not from the server's name, so German 'Alle Nachrichten' is what the sidebar has to fit and 'All mail' is not.
_doc_advance: Per-character advance in em, by class. An estimate and named as one: no font metrics exist in this container, so the test cannot claim pixel truth. The classes come from Roboto's real proportions - i/l/t/punctuation/space are the narrow ones, m/w the wide ones, caps and digits sit between lowercase and wide, and an emoji is drawn about one and a bit em square. Deliberately GENEROUS on lowercase (0.55 against Roboto's ~0.50 mean) so the assertion errs towards calling a label too wide rather than towards passing one that wraps on the phone.

emoji._doc: codepoint > U+2500; U+FE0F (variation selector) draws nothing

_doc_known_wrapping: The labels that STILL do not fit at the chosen width and point size, and are accepted as wrapping. Fitting the widest of them needs a ~384dp sheet, and Material 3 caps a modal drawer at 360dp so a phone keeps a scrim to tap back through; the alternative, an ellipsis, is forbidden - a folder whose name cannot be read is worse than one on two lines. This list is asserted in BOTH directions: a name in it that turns out to fit is stale and fails, and a name outside it that does not fit is a regression and fails.
